issues.legal_issue: A second appeal involving an ownership dispute that requires interpretation of documents raises substantial questions of law that must be decided on the merits.
material_facts: The dispute concerned whether the property belonged to the deceased father or was the defendant’s self-acquired property, with each claim depending on documents and their effect on ownership.
The High Court dismissed the second appeal at the admission stage without examining the documents or framing substantial questions of law.
issues.conclusion: The High Court erred in dismissing the second appeal in limine. The Supreme Court set aside that order and remanded the case for the High Court to frame appropriate substantial questions of law and decide the appeal on its merits.
issues.legal_principle: Under Section 100 of the Code of Civil Procedure, 1908, when a second appeal involves substantial questions of law, the High Court must frame those questions and decide the appeal on the merits after giving notice to the respondents. Interpreting documents and examining their effect involves questions of law; the High Court is therefore required to decide such questions on the merits. No earlier cases are relied on in the judgment.

predicates.second_appeal: The proceeding is a second appeal before a High Court.
predicates.ownership_dispute_requires_document_inte: The dispute over ownership depends on interpreting documents and determining their effect.
predicates.high_court_dismissed_at_admission_withou: The High Court dismissed the second appeal at the admission stage without examining the relevant documents.

issues.definition: When a second appeal concerns ownership that depends on interpreting documents and the High Court dismisses it at admission without examining those documents, the High Court must frame substantial questions of law and decide the appeal on its merits.
